20.I have heard the arguments of Ld. Counsel for the Defendant.

Despite opportunity, neither arguments were led nor were written submissions filed on behalf of the Plaintiff.
21.Before adjudicating the present case, it would be appropriate to discuss the burden of proof required to be discharged in civil proceedings.
It is a settled principle of law that in civil cases, the burden of proof is not as strict as that in criminal cases.
Here, the Plaintiff is required to prove his case only to the standard of preponderance of probabilities.
22.The

burden of proof in civil cases was discussed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Dr.
N.G. Dastane vs Mrs. S. Dastane AIR1975SC1534, wherein it was held as under:

24.Both the issues are taken up together as they are connected.
25.The onus to prove these issues was upon the Plaintiff.
26. Basically, the case of the plaintiff is that the defendants are interfering with the possession of his property, and must be injuncted from doing so.

27.The relief of permanent injunction can be obtained either by proving that the Plaintiff is in lawful possession of the suit property, or by proving that the Plaintiff has better title over the suit property than that of the Defendant.
28.

In this regard, judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court namely Anathula Sudhakar vs. P. Buchi Reddy (2008) 4 SCC 594 becomes relevant, wherein it was held as under:

"In a suit for permanent injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with plaintiff's possession, the plaintiff will have to establish that as on the date of the suit he was in lawful possession of the suit property and defendant tried to interfere or disturb such lawful possession.
Where the property is a building or building with appurtenant land, there may not be much difficulty in establishing possession.
The plaintiff may prove physical or lawful possession, either of himself or by him through his family members or agents or lessees/licensees.

Even in respect of a land without structures,
as for example an agricultural land, possession may be established with reference to the actual use and cultivation.
...But what if the property is a vacant site, which is not physically possessed, used or enjoyed?

In such cases the principle is that possession follows title."

sentences.text: The deemed lapse of land acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 takes place where due to inaction of authorities for five years or more prior to commencement of the said Act, the possession of land has not been taken nor compensation has been paid.
In other words, in case possession has been taken, compensation has not been paid then there is no lapse.
Similarly, if compensation has been paid, possession has not been taken then there is no lapse."

32. Even otherwise, to be entitled to the relief sought, the Plaintiff must establish his physical or lawful possession over the suit property.
However, in the present case, the Plaintiff has failed to establish his possession over the suit property.

The Plaintiff has only relied upon Mark A i.e. copy of khata khatauni, which is not proved as per law, as the plaintiff has merely placed on record a photocopy of khatauni, without calling any witness for proving it.
Furthermore, no document or witness has been brought on record to establish that it is the Plaintiff who is in possession of the suit property.

33.The case of the Plaintiff is further weakened by the fact that in his cross examination, he has stated that he had seen certain documents in PS in the year 2014, executed by his father, in favour of Sh. Ashok Kumar.

Thus, this further creates a doubt in the case put forth by the Plaintiff.
34.The
plaintiff's case also suffers from various inconsistencies.

It is deposed by the plaintiff in his examination in chief that no plot in the share of his father was sold in absence of buyers, therefore,
he kept the land in his possession and constructed some kuccha rooms in various plots.
It is further stated that his share of land being built up, possession of the same was not taken over by the government.
On the contrary, he has stated that he is in lawful 'vacant possession' of the suit property.
Even in the site plan i.e. Ex. PW-1/3 and Ex. PW-1/4, the suit property is shown and marked as a vacant plot.
Also, in photographs relied upon by the plaintiff i.e. PW-1/5, the suit property can be seen to be a vacant plot, upon which, some construction is being carried on.

Thus,
the Plaintiff has even failed to establish the nature of the suit property.
The Plaintiff has made contrary averments in the plaint itself as to whether CS SCJ 535762/2016 Amit Behl vs. Fateh Singh & Ors.

Thus, the case of the Plaintiff suffers from inherent inconsistencies.

35.Thus, in light of the above discussion, the Court has come to the conclusion that the Plaintiff has failed to establish the fact that he is in the possession of the suit property or has any right, title or interest in the suit property.

Since, no document has been adduced by the Plaintiff in the evidence to show his possession over the suit property, the question of defendants interfering in the possession of the Plaintiff does not arise.
36.The case of the Plaintiff is full of inconsistencies.
In view of the court, the Plaintiff has failed to discharge his initial onus.
Therefore, the issue is decided against the Plaintiff and in favour of the Defendant.

Secondly, even if for the sake of arguments, the fact that the possession CS SCJ 535762/2016 Amit Behl vs. Fateh Singh & Ors. Page No.13 of 18 has not been taken over is taken to be true, it is nowhere the case of the Plaintiff that he has not received the compensation, and thus, in light of the above judgment, the proceedings of acquisition would not fail.
Therefore, what comes down from the above discussion is that that the suit property, after acquisition, vests with the government.
32. Even otherwise, to be entitled to the relief sought, the Plaintiff must establish his physical or lawful possession over the suit property.
However, in the present case, the Plaintiff has failed to establish his possession over the suit property.
The Plaintiff has only relied upon Mark A i.e. copy of khata khatauni, which is not proved as per law, as the plaintiff has merely placed on record a photocopy of khatauni, without calling any witness for proving it.
The Plaintiff has made contrary averments in the plaint itself as to whether CS SCJ 535762/2016 Amit Behl vs. Fateh Singh & Ors.
Thus, the case of the Plaintiff suffers from inherent inconsistencies.
Since, no document has been adduced by the Plaintiff in the evidence to show his possession over the suit property, the question of defendants interfering in the possession of the Plaintiff does not arise.
In view of the court, the Plaintiff has failed to discharge his initial onus.
Since the Plaintiff has failed to establish his possession over the suit property, he is not entitled to the relief of permanent injunction.
